name: Solder-Null
geological_features: Surface covered in metallic nodules soldered to bedrock
Impact-scarred wastelands on the sunward hemisphere
Tidally locked hemisphere creating permanent day and night sides
specific_features: Abandoned mining complex on the terminator line
description: Solder-Null is a tidally locked barren world whose sunward face is covered in metallic nodules that appear to have been soldered to the bedrock by the intense radiation, fused into permanent attachment by eons of solar heating. The terminator line is a narrow band where conditions moderate enough for prolonged surface operations, though the transition from eternal day to eternal night creates thermal stresses that fracture the rock into unstable rubble fields. The dark side is a featureless waste of frozen regolith, untouched by light since the planet's rotation locked billions of years ago.

The sunward hemisphere blazes with reflected light from millions of metallic nodules, each one a natural alloy of iron, copper, and trace platinum that has been heat-fused to its surroundings. The dark side is the opposite in every way: cold, dark, and utterly still, a frozen mirror image of the molten-bright daylight face. The terminator line feels like standing between two different worlds, one foot in light and heat, the other in darkness and cold, with the grinding sound of thermal fracture as a constant companion.

A mining operation on the terminator line extracted metallic nodules from the sunward side for several years before the logistics of operating on a tidally locked world with no atmosphere proved unsustainable. The operation left behind processing equipment, habitat modules, and a partially excavated trench that revealed the nodule layer extends to a depth of at least fifty meters, far more material than was initially estimated. The bedrock beneath the nodules shows unusual crystalline patterns that do not match standard geological models.

The platinum content of the nodules makes Solder-Null potentially valuable despite its hostile conditions, and advances in autonomous mining technology have renewed interest in exploitation. The abandoned infrastructure on the terminator line provides a foundation for any future operation. The crystalline bedrock patterns have attracted geological interest, as they suggest the planet may have undergone an unusual formation process, possibly involving the same ancient impact event that deposited the metallic material now fused to its surface.
